tasks.short: Assess the registration fee and file it.

steps.what: Assess the fee related to those property documents.
Accept the registration fee they assess.
File the registration fee they assess.

tasks.design: The examiner assesses the fee related to the property documents and accepts it. {DOCS} only shows the published registration fee, then files the fee they accepted. The table does not choose the fee. If the table has no row, they assess it themselves and the lookup stays unused.
tasks.previous_blocker: A published fee was looked up in a paper table before the examiner could assess which one applied.
tasks.enabler_now: A published fee the office already holds can be shown by document type.
tasks.still_hard: Which fee applies to these documents stays with the examiner.
tasks.human_edge: The examiner assesses the fee. A table does not.
tasks.altitude: The assessment and the acceptance stay in full. Only showing the published fee and filing the accepted fee are shorter.

reach.task: Hear the fee the examiner assessed
reach.learn: The table does not choose the fee

evidence.claim: A published fee can be shown. Which fee applies is the examiner's assessment.
National rules differ on who may register a document and on which legislation applies. The examiner determines whether it can be registered. This file does not register it.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a property document needs a registration fee and ends when the accepted fee is filed. The examiner assesses which fee applies. The table does not choose it.

The fields are document type and the published fee name. The fee table produces the published amount. The examiner produces which fee applies. If the table has no row, they assess it themselves and the lookup stays unused.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the assessment stays. The lookup and the filing are the parts that move.
unknowns: Whether a published fee row exists for every document type they register.
Which fees the office assesses with no published row.
research_questions: Does a published fee row exist for every document type they register?
Which fees does the office assess with no published row?

already_counted.description: The whole step stays with the title examiner
The whole step stays with the title examiner

incremental.description: Keep the table to published registration fees

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the table has no row, the lookup stays unused, and the low end is the assessment, which stays either way. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The examiner still assesses which registration fee applies. A published fee can be shown. The table does not choose it.
reach: A presenter hears the fee the examiner assessed
skills_to_grow: Assessing the fee when the table has no row
role.ambitious_version: Every fee that is filed is one the examiner assessed.
